exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating a Quotient of Two Polynomials

question.explanation:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x) = x$ and $v(x) = 1 - x^{2},$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

\begin{align} u'(x)& = 1, \\ v'(x) &= -2x. \end{align}

Applying the quotient rule, we have

\[ \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x) \cdot v'(x)} {[v(x)]^2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1\cdot \left(1 - x^{2}\right) - x\cdot(-2x)}{\left( 1 - x^{2} \right)^2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{ 1 - x^{2} + 2x^{2} }{\left( 1 - x^{2} \right)^{2}}\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{ 1 + x^{2} }{\left( 1 - x^{2} \right)^{2}}}. } \]

example.title: Differentiating a Quotient of Two Polynomials

question.explanation:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x) = 5x^2$ and $v(x) = 9x-7,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

\begin{align} u'(x)& =10x, \\ v'(x) &= 9. \end{align}

\[ \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x) v'(x)} {[v(x)]^2}\\[3pt] &=\dfrac{10x\cdot\left( 9x-7 \right ) -(5x^2)\cdot 9}{\left( 9x-7\right)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{90x^2-70x-45x^2}{\left( 9x-7\right)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{45x^2-70x}{\left( 9x - 7\right)^2}. } \]

example.title: Differentiating a Quotient of Two Polynomials

question.explanation:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x) = 9x - 3$ and $v(x) = 2x,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

\begin{align} u'(x) &= 9, \\ v'(x) &= 2. \end{align}

Applying the quotient rule, we have

\[ \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x) \cdot v'(x)} {[v(x)]^2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{9\cdot 2x - (9x - 3)\cdot 2}{\left( 2x \right)^2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{18x - 18x + 6}{4x^{2}} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{6}{4x^{2}} \\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{3}{2x^{2}}}. } \]

example.title: Differentiating a Quotient of Two Polynomials

question.explanation:
The numerator and denominator are $u(x) = -3$ and $v(x) = 4x - 5,$ respectively. Their derivatives are given by

\begin{align} u'(x)& =0, \\ v'(x) &= 4. \end{align}

Applying the quotient rule, we have

\[ \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x) \cdot v'(x)} {[v(x)]^2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{0\cdot\left( 4x - 5 \right ) - (-3)\cdot 4}{\left( 4x - 5 \right)^2}\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{12}{\left( 4x - 5 \right)^2}}. } \]

exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating a Quotient Containing Other Functions

question.explanation:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\dfrac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x) = \sin{x}$ and $v(x) = 5^{x}.$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac{u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x)\cdot v'(x)}{[v(x)]^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{(\sin{x})' \cdot 5^{x} - \sin{x} \cdot (5^{x})'}{\left(5^{x}\right)^2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\cos{x} \cdot 5^{x} - \sin{x} \cdot 5^{x}\ln{5}} {\left(5^{x}\right)^{2}} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{5^{x}\left(\cos{x} - \sin{x}\ln{5}\right)}{\left(5^{x}\right)^{2}} \\[5pt] & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{\cos{x} - \sin{x}\ln{5}}{5^{x}}} \end{align}

example.title: Differentiating a Quotient Containing Other Functions

question.text: If a curve $\mathcal C$ is given by $y=\dfrac{\cos x }{1+\sin x},$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x= \dfrac \pi 2.$
question.explanation:
In this case, the expression for $y$ is a quotient $\dfrac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x) =\cos x$ and $v(x) =1+\sin x.$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: \[ \eqalign{ f'(x ) &= \dfrac{u'(x)\cdot v(x) - u(x)\cdot v'(x)}{[v(x)]^2}\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{(\cos x)' \cdot(1+\sin x) - \cos x \cdot (1+\sin x)'}{(1+\sin x)^2} \\[3pt] & = \dfrac{(-\sin x)(1+\sin x) - (\cos x)\cos x}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\[3pt] &=\dfrac{(-\sin x-\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x)}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\[3pt] &=\dfrac{(-\sin x-(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x))}{(1+\sin x)^2} } \] Since $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x=1$, we have

\[ \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac{(-\sin x-1)}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{-(1+\sin x)}{(1+\sin x)^2}\\ &=-\dfrac{1}{1+\sin x}. } \]

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ into the formula and get \begin{align} f'\left(\dfrac \pi 2\right) & = -\dfrac{1}{1+\sin\left(\dfrac \pi 2\right)} \\ & = -\dfrac{1}{1+1} \\ & = -\dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align}

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-\dfrac{1}{2}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating a Quotient Using Leibniz Notation

question.explanation:
Let $u = \log_{3}{x} = \dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{3}}$ and $v = x^2.$ Then \begin{align} \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac{1}{x\ln{3}} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = 2x. \end{align}

Using the quotient rule, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac{ v\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}-u\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}}{v^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left( x^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x\ln{3}} - \dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{3}} \cdot 2x \right)} {(x^2)^2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left( \dfrac{x}{\ln{3}} - \dfrac{2x\ln{x}}{\ln{3}} \right)} {x^4} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x - 2x\ln{x}}{x^4 \ln{3}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x(1 - 2\ln{x})}{x^4 \ln{3}}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1 - 2\ln{x}}{x^3 \ln{3}}\\[5pt] & = \Big( \, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{1 - 2\ln{x}} \, \Big) \cdot \dfrac{1}{x^3\ln{3}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Differentiating a Quotient Using Leibniz Notation

question.explanation:
Let $u=x^{2}$ and $v=2^{x}.$ Then

\begin{align} \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}&=2x \qquad \text{and} \qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}=2^{x}\ln{2}. \end{align}

Using the quotient rule, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} & = \dfrac{ v\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}-u\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}}{v^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac { 2^{x} \cdot 2x - x^2 \cdot 2^{x}\ln{2} } {\left(2^{x}\right)^2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {2^{x} \cdot x\left(2 - x \ln{2}\right) } {\left(2^{x}\right)^{2}} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x\left(2 - x \ln{2}\right) }{2^{x}} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{x}{2^x} \cdot \Big( \, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2 - x \ln{2}} \, \Big). \end{align*}
